prompt: A citizen services team needs a guided, low-code path to define tables, forms, and roles for a new permit-tracking application without writing boilerplate configuration by hand. Which tool should they start with?
choices: Direct edits to global system tables without an application scope boundary
A spreadsheet import that bypasses dictionary and form generation entirely
App Engine Studio to create the scoped application with guided data and UI design
A standalone IDE project deployed outside the instance with no platform integration
explanation: App Engine Studio provides a guided low-code workspace to design scoped applications, including tables, forms, roles, and related artifacts in one flow.

prompt: Facilities management wants a Facilities Request application whose tables and scripts stay isolated from HR and IT apps, with access granted only when another team explicitly allows it. What should they create?
choices: A report dashboard that reads HR tables without an application boundary
A scoped application in its own application scope with a private namespace for its artifacts
A set of global tables prefixed with u_ that any administrator can modify freely
A UI page only, with no backing table or application file structure
explanation: A scoped application provides namespace isolation so other applications cannot access its tables and logic unless cross-scope privileges are granted.

prompt: You are modeling work orders that share assignment, priority, and state fields with the Task table but also need custom asset-specific columns. Which data-model approach reuses Task behavior while adding fields?
choices: Extend the Task table so the new table inherits standard task fields and adds its own
Duplicate every Task column manually on a standalone table with no parent link
Store work-order details in a single HTML field on the User table
Create a Journal field on Task and paste JSON payloads for each work order
explanation: Table extension creates a child table that inherits the parent table's fields and behavior while allowing additional custom fields.

prompt: After building a custom inventory application, users cannot find its lists and forms in the Application Navigator. Which artifact should you configure to expose navigation entries?
choices: A business rule that runs on insert to create navigator entries automatically
A transform map that copies module records from the Incident application
A UI macro attached to the homepage that replaces the Application Navigator
An application menu with modules that link to lists, forms, or other content
explanation: Application menus group modules that appear in the Application Navigator and route users to the application's lists, forms, and other content.

prompt: An Inspection record must point to exactly one Building record so inspectors can open the building form from the inspection. Which field type should you add on the Inspection table?
choices: A Reference field on Inspection that points to the Building table
A Duration field on Inspection that stores the inspection elapsed time only
A Password2 field on Inspection that encrypts the building identifier text
A String field on Building that stores comma-separated inspection numbers
explanation: A reference field stores a pointer to a single record on another table, enabling one-to-many relationships and form navigation via the reference.

prompt: A vendor-delivered scoped app must protect its Script Includes from direct use by unrelated applications on the same instance. What does application scope enforce by default?
choices: Every user in the instance receives implicit write access to all scoped tables
Other scopes cannot access the application's tables and server scripts unless granted permission
Client scripts in one scope can call any Script Include in another scope without restriction
Scoped tables are automatically copied into the global namespace on every upgrade
explanation: Scoped applications isolate their artifacts; cross-scope access requires explicit privileges rather than open global access.

prompt: Your team debates building a small departmental tool inside the global scope versus a dedicated scoped application. When is a scoped application the better design choice?
choices: When the change must modify core platform tables without any namespace boundary
When you only need a one-off UI page with no persistent data model
When the solution ships as a reusable package with its own tables, ACLs, and lifecycle
When developers want every script to run with unrestricted global table access
explanation: Scoped applications suit packaged solutions with isolated artifacts, controlled access, and independent versioning compared to ad hoc global changes.

prompt: A procurement team needs human-readable request numbers such as PRQ0001001 generated automatically on insert. Which field configuration meets this requirement?
choices: A URL field that stores an external numbering service link for each record
A choice field whose values are manually typed by agents for every new request
A floating-point field with no auto-numbering or prefix configuration applied
A string field with Number maintenance enabled and a prefix defined for the table
explanation: Number maintenance on a string field auto-generates sequential values with an optional prefix when records are created.

prompt: An asset record must relate to multiple configuration items, and each configuration item may relate to many assets. Which relationship pattern fits this many-to-many need?
choices: A many-to-many relationship using an intermediate M2M table between the two tables
A Journal field on Asset where technicians paste comma-separated CI names
A Document ID field on Asset that uploads a PDF list of related configuration items
A single Reference field on Asset that stores only one configuration item at a time
explanation: Many-to-many relationships use an intermediate table so each side can associate with multiple records on the other table.

prompt: Business users report that the label on a custom field does not match their process terminology on forms and lists. Where should a developer update the displayed field label?
choices: The client script onLoad handler, hard-coding a new label string on every visit
The dictionary entry for the field on the table, updating the Column label property
The system property com.snc.label.override, which replaces all field labels globally
The related list layout, which overrides dictionary labels for form fields only
explanation: Field labels are defined on dictionary entries; updating the Column label changes how the field appears on forms and lists.

prompt: After several teams publish scoped apps from App Engine Studio, operations needs a central place to review versions, dependencies, and installation status across instances. Which console should they use?
choices: The system scheduler to batch-delete unused application records nightly
A custom UI page that queries the User table for application ownership only
Workflow Studio to redesign approval flows for each published application
App Engine Management Center to monitor and manage scoped applications centrally
explanation: App Engine Management Center provides centralized visibility into scoped applications, versions, and deployment status across the environment.

prompt: A change request table must appear in Incident-related reports while keeping its own unique fields. The team already extended Task for assignment fields. What is the effect of extending Change Request from Task?
choices: Change Request inherits Task fields and behaviors while supporting additional custom columns
Change Request disables polymorphic queries so records never appear in Task lists
Change Request stores data only in Task and cannot have its own dictionary entries
Change Request replaces the Task table and deletes existing task records on save
explanation: An extended table inherits parent fields and can add its own; records remain queryable through the parent where configured.

prompt: A status field should offer a fixed set of values—Draft, Review, Approved—without linking to another table. Which field type is appropriate?
choices: A Reference field pointing to the User table for each status value
A Choice field with defined options stored on the dictionary entry
A Password field that stores hashed status tokens for each selection
A Glide Duration field measured in days since the record was created
explanation: Choice fields provide a fixed list of values on the same table without requiring a related table or reference relationship.

prompt: Which naming convention applies to tables created inside a scoped application with vendor prefix acme?
choices: Tables inherit the literal name task with no scope identifier in the table name
Tables must use the global u_ prefix regardless of application scope
Tables use the scope prefix such as x_acme_ followed by the table name
Tables are stored only in memory and never receive a persistent table name
explanation: Scoped application tables include the application scope prefix in the table name, such as x_vendor_app_table.

prompt: A facilities approval process needs drag-and-drop flow design with activities, conditions, and notifications tied to scoped application records. Which tool should the team use?
choices: A related list on the User table that lists pending approvals alphabetically
A transform map that copies approval states from Incident on every insert
A client script onSubmit handler that sends email without any flow definition
Workflow Studio to model the approval flow with activities and conditions visually
explanation: Workflow Studio provides visual flow design for approvals and automation activities integrated with platform records.

prompt: Users open a Company form and expect to see related Active Contracts in a subordinate list filtered to that company. Which configuration exposes the related records on the form?
choices: A related list on the Company form showing Contract records where company matches
A homepage module that opens all contracts without filtering by company
A business rule on Contract that deletes records not linked to the open Company
A UI Policy that copies contract numbers into a string field on Company
explanation: Related lists display associated records on a form based on reference or other configured relationships between tables.

prompt: A scoped application table must be readable at runtime by an integration in another scope during record queries. Which setting controls runtime access to scoped tables?
choices: The Column label on each field, which grants read access to external scopes
The auto-number prefix, which determines whether other scopes can query rows
Runtime Access to Application Tables configured on the application record
The module order in the Application Navigator, which sets query privileges
explanation: Runtime Access to Application Tables defines whether other scopes can read scoped application tables at runtime.

prompt: A developer finished building a scoped app in App Engine Studio and needs to move it to a test instance for user acceptance. What is the recommended packaging path?
choices: Publish or export the scoped application and install it on the target instance
Manually retype every dictionary entry on the test instance without a package
Copy individual User records from production to carry the application logic
Disable application scope on production so tables become global automatically
explanation: Scoped applications are published or exported as application packages and installed on target instances rather than copied record by record.

prompt: Agents need a form button that runs client-side logic and then calls the server to update a related record without leaving the form. Which artifact combination fits this behavior?
choices: A data policy that blocks all updates until the user refreshes the browser
A related list export that downloads CSV data when the button is pressed
A scheduled job that polls the form every minute for button clicks
A UI Action with a client script handler that may call GlideAjax for server work
explanation: UI Actions can expose form buttons whose client scripts perform client logic and invoke GlideAjax to execute server-side code.

prompt: Stakeholders want the Request form split into sections—Details, Approval, Closure—with fields grouped for readability. Where should the developer arrange section layout?
choices: The business rule insert condition, which renders sections based on state
The ACL read rule, which determines which sections each role can see
The form layout and form sections configured for the table's form view
The list layout, which controls section headers on the record form only
explanation: Form sections and layout on the table's form view control how fields are grouped and displayed on the record form.

prompt: When a user opens a new Hire record, the Start Date field should default to today's date before any edits occur. Which client script type and timing apply?
choices: An onLoad client script that sets the field value when the form first renders
An onSubmit client script that runs after the record is saved to the database
A before Business Rule that executes only when the list view first loads
A UI Policy with no condition that runs exclusively during list filtering
explanation: onLoad client scripts run when the form loads, making them appropriate for initializing field values before user interaction.

prompt: Before a Safety Inspection form can be submitted, the developer must block save when Required PPE is empty and show an error message to the user. Which approach handles this pre-submit validation on the client?
choices: A UI Policy set to read-only on Required PPE, which prevents empty values on save
A before Business Rule that displays a client alert before the form loads
An onChange script on an unrelated field that hides the Submit button permanently
An onSubmit client script that checks the field and returns false to cancel submit
explanation: onSubmit client scripts validate immediately before submission; returning false cancels the save and allows displaying a message to the user.

prompt: A client script must hide the Contract Value field when Type is Internal and show it when Type is External during user edits. Which client API object controls visibility and mandatory state on the form?
choices: g_form methods such as setVisible and setMandatory on the target fields
GlideRecord on the client to update sys_ui_form records during onChange
GlideSystem hasRole to replace field widgets with static text labels
gs.getProperty to read instance properties and rewrite the form HTML tree
explanation: The g_form object provides client-side methods to show, hide, and set mandatory state on form fields during script execution.

prompt: On the Incident form, when Category is set to Safety, the Work Notes field must become mandatory without writing script. Which configuration enforces that declaratively?
choices: A client script onLoad that deletes Work Notes when Category equals Safety
A UI Policy with condition Category is Safety that sets Work Notes to mandatory
A data policy on the User table that mirrors Category values to Work Notes
A before Business Rule that rejects inserts unless Work Notes is populated
explanation: UI Policies declaratively set fields mandatory, read-only, or visible based on conditions without requiring client scripting.

prompt: A client script needs the server to calculate a risk score from several fields and return the result without reloading the page. Which client-side pattern should the developer use?
choices: GlideAjax calling a client-callable Script Include that computes and returns the score
A synchronous GlideRecord query executed directly in the browser onSubmit handler
A UI Policy action script that posts the entire form to an external REST endpoint
A scheduled script that emails the score to the user after the form is closed
explanation: GlideAjax invokes a client-callable Script Include on the server and returns data asynchronously to the client script.

prompt: When Priority changes on an open Task, the client script must compare the previous value to the new value and warn if the user downgrades from Critical. Which onChange parameter supplies the prior field value?
choices: The newValue parameter, which always contains the value from the prior save
The isLoading flag, which stores the last saved database row as text
The control object, which returns the previous choice label as a number
The oldValue parameter passed to the onChange client script handler
explanation: onChange client scripts receive oldValue and newValue parameters; oldValue holds the field value before the user's change.

prompt: A developer must pick server-side enforcement for validating a field value on insert and client-side hiding of a field when a checkbox is cleared. Select the two mechanisms that match each need.
choices: A before Business Rule to validate the field value during database insert
A UI Policy to execute a GlideRecord query against an external database
A client script onSubmit to permanently delete related records on the server
A UI Policy to hide the dependent field when the checkbox condition is false
explanation: Business Rules run server-side on database events for validation; UI Policies declaratively control field visibility on the client based on conditions.

prompt: An onChange client script should skip custom logic while the form is still loading initial values from the server. Which parameter indicates the form load state?
choices: The oldValue parameter, which equals true only during the first paint event
The isLoading parameter, which is true while the form is loading record data
The GlideAjax response status code returned before onChange fires
The g_form.isNewRecord method, which returns loading status for every field
explanation: The isLoading parameter in onChange scripts is true during initial form load, allowing scripts to avoid running logic prematurely.

prompt: A catalog item uses a variable set; when Variable A is Yes, Variable B must become read-only on the item form. Which client-side artifact supports catalog variable behavior?
choices: A transform map on sc_cat_item that sets variables read-only after order submit
A table-level UI Policy on sys_user, which controls catalog variable widgets
A catalog client script with onChange logic against the catalog item variables
A MID Server script that polls variable values and locks fields remotely
explanation: Catalog client scripts run against catalog item variables and can set visibility or read-only state based on variable changes.

prompt: Managers want a Resolve button on the Case form visible only when State is Active and the user holds the case_manager role. Which form artifact supports conditional button display?
choices: A related list script that injects HTML buttons into the form footer
A business rule on update that renames the form title to Resolve
A UI Policy that converts the Submit button into a Resolve button globally
A UI Action with a condition involving State and role checks before display
explanation: UI Actions support conditions on form context and roles to control when custom buttons appear and execute.

prompt: When Approval Status is Pending, the Resolution Code field should be hidden; when Approved, it should appear. No scripting is desired. Which configuration applies?
choices: A client script onLoad that removes Resolution Code from the dictionary entry
A list layout change that hides Resolution Code on the form view permanently
A UI Policy with conditions on Approval Status that toggles Resolution Code visibility
A before Business Rule that sets Resolution Code to null on every save attempt
explanation: UI Policies can declaratively show or hide fields based on form conditions without writing client scripts.

prompt: An onSubmit client script must display a confirmation dialog when Estimated Cost exceeds 50000 and cancel submit if the user declines. Which approach meets that requirement?
choices: Call confirm() with the warning text, then return false when the user cancels
Call g_form.addInfoMessage or showErrorBox, which always wait for OK and Cancel
Call gs.addInfoMessage in the client script, which blocks submit until the user replies
Call current.setAbortAction in the onSubmit script to halt client-side rendering
explanation: Client scripts use the browser confirm() dialog for OK/Cancel prompts. Returning false from onSubmit cancels the submission when the user declines. g_form messaging methods show informational or field errors but do not present a confirmation dialog that waits for cancel.

prompt: A GlideAjax call returns both a scalar score and a reference to a risk catalog record. Which methods retrieve those response parts on the client?
choices: getXML for scalar values and getTableName for every reference returned synchronously
getStatus for scores and getRowCount for reference payloads exclusively
getParameter for scores and getChoiceLabel for catalog references only
getAnswer for scalar values and getReference for reference fields returned by the Script Include
explanation: GlideAjax response objects expose getAnswer for simple return values and getReference for reference field payloads from Script Includes.

prompt: A UI Policy makes Assignment Group mandatory when Category is Hardware. When Category changes away from Hardware, mandatory should be removed automatically. Which policy setting supports reversing actions?
choices: Set the policy to run on server only so mandatory state never clears
Add a second UI Policy with an empty condition that runs on list load
Enable Reverse if false so actions undo when the condition no longer matches
Disable the UI Policy entirely and rely on a nightly scheduled job instead
explanation: Reverse if false on a UI Policy removes applied actions when the condition becomes false, restoring prior field state.

prompt: An onSubmit client script validates that Close Notes is populated for closed states. If validation fails, the record must not save. What must the script return?
choices: Return the string cancel so the UI Policy engine blocks the business rule
Return false after showing a message so the platform cancels the submit operation
Return true after calling current.setAbortAction on the client GlideRecord object
Return null so the server decides whether to ignore the validation failure
explanation: onSubmit client scripts return false to prevent form submission when client-side validation fails.

prompt: A form requirement can be met either by a UI Policy or a client script, but the team prefers maintainability and upgrade safety for simple show-or-hide logic. Which approach should they choose?
choices: A UI Policy because declarative conditions avoid custom script maintenance for simple field behavior
A client script because UI Policies cannot target individual fields on a form
A business rule because show-or-hide logic must always execute on the server insert
A data policy because it is the only artifact that runs before the form renders
explanation: UI Policies handle straightforward field visibility and mandatory rules declaratively, reducing script maintenance for simple form behavior.

prompt: Contractors should read Contract records but never create or delete them. Which ACL design on the Contract table supports that?
choices: A single write ACL that implicitly grants read, create, update, and delete together
A client script that sets g_form.setReadOnly true, which replaces table ACL evaluation
A table read ACL that includes the contractor role, without granting create or delete to that role
A UI Policy on Contract that hides the New button and therefore removes delete rights
explanation: ACLs are evaluated per operation. Granting read for the contractor role allows viewing records; create and delete remain denied when those users do not pass create/delete ACL conditions. Client scripts and UI Policies do not replace table ACL evaluation for record operations.

prompt: Only users with the catalog_admin role should configure catalog items in a scoped application. Which security artifact ties catalog item records to that role?
choices: Client scripts that check role names and skip ACL evaluation when a match is found
Dictionary read-only flags that substitute for role-based access control entirely
Roles referenced on ACLs or embedded in role conditions that guard catalog tables and related records
Module order numbers that automatically grant admin rights to the first module viewer
explanation: Roles are assigned to users and referenced in ACL conditions to restrict operations on tables and related resources.

prompt: Salary Amount on the Employee table must be visible only to HR payroll staff, while other Employee fields remain readable more broadly. Which ACL granularity applies?
choices: A business rule that clears Salary Amount before non-HR users open the form
A field-level ACL on the Salary Amount column with a role or scripted condition
A table ACL on Employee that grants full access to every column for all users
A UI Policy that hides Salary Amount, which replaces the need for field ACLs
explanation: Field-level ACLs restrict access to specific columns independently of table-level read permissions.

prompt: An integration in Scope B queries a table owned by Scope A and receives an security constraint error despite valid credentials. What is the most likely cause?
choices: Scope B lacks cross-scope privilege to access Scope A tables or Script Includes at runtime
The integration user lacks a UI Policy that enables GlideAjax on the target table
The table dictionary label is missing, which blocks all cross-scope GlideRecord queries
Application menus from Scope A are unpublished, which denies every database read
explanation: Cross-scope access requires explicit privileges; scoped applications isolate data and server artifacts from other scopes by default.

prompt: Scope B must call a Script Include in Scope A from GlideAjax and read rows from a Scope A table at runtime. Select the two platform settings that typically must be in place.
choices: Cross-scope privilege allowing Scope B to access Scope A Script Includes marked client callable
A UI Policy in Scope A that makes every field visible to anonymous users globally
Disabling application scope on Scope A so all artifacts move into the global namespace
Runtime access or table ACL design permitting Scope B to read the Scope A table as required
explanation: Cross-scope Script Include access requires explicit cross-scope privileges; reading scoped tables from another scope requires runtime access configuration and appropriate ACLs.

prompt: A user can open a form but receives Access denied when submitting an update even though a read ACL passes. Which evaluation order concept explains this behavior?
choices: Read ACLs automatically grant write access whenever the user can open the form
ACLs are evaluated per operation, so write ACLs can deny updates even when read ACLs allow viewing
Business rules execute before ACLs and therefore bypass write denial on submit
UI Policies run after all ACL checks and can override denied write operations
explanation: Each ACL operation—read, write, create, delete—is evaluated independently; passing read does not imply write permission.

prompt: A developer needs to install, upgrade, and configure application files within one scoped application without full admin rights on the entire instance. Which role model supports delegated app ownership?
choices: The itil role, which automatically grants write access to every scoped table
The global admin role only, because scoped applications cannot define their own roles
The scoped application's admin or delegated developer role defined for that application scope
The report_user role, which includes application installation privileges
explanation: Scoped applications define roles such as admin for delegated management of that application's artifacts within the scope boundary.

prompt: Analysts may edit open Project records but must not delete them. Which ACL operations should you configure separately on the Project table?
choices: Rely on a client script that hides Delete and assume server delete checks are unnecessary
Disable the Project table ACLs entirely and enforce rules with UI Policies only
Grant a single ACL labeled admin that covers read, write, create, and delete together
Grant write ACL for updates while using a delete ACL that does not grant delete permission
explanation: Write and delete are distinct ACL operations; allowing updates does not require allowing record deletion.

prompt: Scope B needs to invoke a protected Script Include in Scope A from a client script via GlideAjax. An administrator must grant access without moving the include to global scope. What should they configure?
choices: Cross-scope privilege on Scope A allowing Scope B to access the client-callable Script Include
A data policy on Scope A that marks the Script Include as a dictionary attribute
Runtime access to tables only, which automatically exposes all Script Includes cross-scope
A UI Action in Scope B that copies the Script Include source into a global business rule
explanation: Cross-scope privileges explicitly allow another application scope to access designated Script Includes while keeping them in the owning scope.

prompt: A user with the app_user role opens a custom module in the Application Navigator but receives Access Denied when the list loads. Module roles are configured correctly. What should you investigate first?
choices: Whether the module label color is set to default
Whether the record producer variable order is alphabetical
Whether a table ACL denies read on the underlying table for that role
Whether the homepage gauge cache needs clearing
explanation: Module roles control navigator visibility; table ACLs control record access. A user can see a module yet fail read ACL checks on the target table.

prompt: While troubleshooting field-level access, you enable Security debugging and impersonate the affected user. The debug log shows the table ACL passed but the field ACL failed. What does this indicate?
choices: The user can access the record but the specific field is restricted
The admin role was denied at the table level
ACL evaluation skipped the table entirely
Client scripts blocked the form before ACLs ran
explanation: ACLs evaluate from general to specific; passing the table ACL but failing the field ACL means the record is readable but that field is protected.

prompt: A developer creates a new ACL and needs to confirm it grants read access to app_user but not to guest. Which verification approach is most reliable?
choices: Delete all other ACLs on the table to isolate the new rule
Disable the login page so only admins can authenticate
Convert the table to global scope and retest
Impersonate app_user, attempt the read, then impersonate guest and confirm denial
explanation: Impersonating representative users and attempting the operation confirms ACL behavior without relying on admin bypass.

prompt: An ACL requires the itil role and includes a condition that current.state == 1. A user with itil opens a record where state is 2. Will the ACL grant access?
choices: No, because both the role and the condition must be satisfied
No, because ACL conditions only apply to delete operations
Yes, because conditions are ignored when a role is specified
Yes, because holding the role alone is sufficient
explanation: An ACL grants access only when required roles, conditions, and scripts (if present) all evaluate successfully.

prompt: You must limit who can install and configure a scoped application without granting full admin. Which artifact enforces application-level access?
choices: A transform map coalesce field on sys_app
A dictionary override on sys_scope
Roles assigned on the application record and its modules
A Flow Designer schedule trigger
explanation: Application and module role requirements restrict who can access application configuration and navigation without full admin rights.

prompt: A business rule in scope x_acme_app calls new x_other_app.Utils().calculate() and fails with a cross-scope access error. What must an administrator configure?
choices: A new inbound email action in x_other_app
An import set staging table shared between scopes
A UI Policy on the Utils Script Include form
A cross-scope access privilege authorizing x_acme_app to access the x_other_app Script Include
explanation: Scoped applications cannot call another scope's Script Includes at runtime unless a cross-scope (restricted caller) access privilege explicitly authorizes that access. Runtime Access to Application Tables controls table data access, not Script Include execution across scopes.

prompt: During delegated development, an admin wants vendor developers to edit business rules and client scripts but not ACLs in a scoped app. Which capability supports this?
choices: Removing all roles from the application menu
Disabling source control for the instance
Delegated Development file-type permissions scoped to the application
Converting the application to global scope
explanation: Delegated Development lets admins grant developers rights to specific application file types while protecting other artifacts.

prompt: Which record operations can an Access Control rule restrict on a table? (Choose two.)
choices: report
create
delete
execute
explanation: ACLs secure CRUD-style operations such as create, read, write, and delete. Execute and report are not ACL operation types.

prompt: A field-level ACL on u_priority exists alongside a table ACL on the same table. A user passes the table read ACL but fails on the field. Which evaluation order explains this?
choices: Table ACL is evaluated first, then the more specific field ACL
Only the field ACL is evaluated for list views
Field ACLs are skipped when a table ACL exists
ACLs are evaluated in alphabetical order by name
explanation: ServiceNow evaluates ACLs from most general to most specific; users must pass both table and field ACLs to read a protected field.

prompt: A developer must stamp u_requested_by with the current user before a new record is written to the database. Which Business Rule timing is appropriate?
choices: after insert, with After checked
async, with Advanced checked only
display, with Before and After both checked
before insert, with Before checked
explanation: Before insert/update business rules run prior to the database commit, allowing field values to be set before the record is saved.

prompt: Before saving an incident, a developer needs to recalculate u_sla_due from priority and category without waiting for the transaction to finish. Which configuration meets the requirement?
choices: A before business rule on insert and update that sets u_sla_due on current
An onLoad client script that writes directly to the database
A UI Policy that queues an async event after save
An after business rule that runs only on display
explanation: Before business rules execute during the save transaction before commit, making them the right place to set field values prior to persistence.

prompt: After a change request is inserted, a business rule must notify an external monitoring system without delaying the user's save response. Which approach fits best?
choices: A before business rule that performs a synchronous REST call
An async after business rule that calls a Script Include to send the notification
An onSubmit client script that calls RESTMessageV2 directly
A display business rule that blocks the form until the call completes
explanation: Async after business rules run in a separate transaction after commit, avoiding delays to the user while performing follow-up work.

prompt: A nightly job must purge closed task records older than 90 days. Which artifact should the developer configure?
choices: A UI Policy that hides old records from lists
An onChange client script on the task table
A Scheduled Job with a daily or periodic run executing a server script
A Flow Designer record trigger set to onLoad
explanation: Scheduled Jobs run server-side logic on defined schedules, suitable for recurring maintenance such as record cleanup.

prompt: How should a developer register a custom event x_app.record.approved so notifications and script actions can subscribe to it?
choices: Define the event in a UI Policy action script
Store the event payload in g_scratchpad on the client
Add the event name as a dictionary column on the table
Create an Event Registry entry and fire it with gs.eventQueue() from server code
explanation: Custom events are declared in the Event Registry and triggered with gs.eventQueue(); subscribers include notifications and script actions.

prompt: Which low-code tool lets a developer build multi-step automation with record triggers, approvals, and subflows without writing full workflow code?
choices: Flow Designer
Access Control rule builder
Dictionary Entry editor
Form Designer
explanation: Flow Designer provides a visual, low-code interface for building flows with triggers, actions, approvals, and reusable subflows.

prompt: In a before business rule, which call queues the registered event x_app.task.closed for the current record?
choices: gs.eventQueue('x_app.task.closed', current, parm1, parm2)
current.eventQueue('x_app.task.closed')
g_form.eventQueue('x_app.task.closed')
gs.getProperty('x_app.task.closed')
explanation: gs.eventQueue(name, GlideRecord, parm1, parm2) fires a registered event tied to a record so subscribers can react asynchronously.

prompt: When a facilities request moves to Approved, stakeholders need email with record details. Which artifact defines recipients, subject, and body?
choices: An ACL script on the facilities table
A transform map field map
A dictionary attribute on the state field
A Notification record triggered by a condition or event on the table
explanation: Notification records define when to send email (condition or event), who receives it, and the message content including mail scripts.

prompt: Where should reusable server-side helper functions for a scoped application live so business rules and flows can call them?
choices: A Script Include class in the application scope
The notification email footer template
A UI Policy action on each table
An onChange client script on every form
explanation: Script Includes encapsulate reusable server-side logic that other server scripts, business rules, and flows can instantiate and call.

prompt: Email sent to the instance must create task records from parsed message content. Which component processes inbound messages?
choices: Outbound REST Message
Transform Map script
Inbound Email Action
UI Policy
explanation: Inbound Email Actions parse received email and execute scripts to create or update records based on message content.

prompt: Which Business Rule configurations run logic after the database transaction commits? (Choose two.)
choices: After insert with After checked
Before update with Before checked
Async with Advanced checked
Display with Display checked
explanation: After business rules run following commit; async business rules also execute after commit in a separate transaction. Before rules run prior to commit.

prompt: Three flows share identical approval routing steps. How can the developer avoid duplicating those steps in each flow?
choices: Copy the same action blocks manually into every flow version
Add the steps as conditions on table ACLs
Store the steps in an onLoad client script
Build a Subflow with defined inputs and outputs and call it from each flow
explanation: Subflows package reusable steps with inputs and outputs so multiple parent flows can invoke the same logic.

prompt: A flow must start whenever a u_request record is created with state Requested. Which trigger type should the developer select?
choices: UI Policy trigger on the request form
Scheduled Job Day-of-month field
Record Created trigger on u_request with a matching condition
Inbound email trigger on the instance mailbox
explanation: Record Created triggers fire flows when new records are inserted on the specified table, optionally filtered by condition.

prompt: A team wants a reusable Flow Designer step that calls a Script Include and returns a status code to downstream actions. What should they create?
choices: An import set staging table
A custom Action with defined inputs, steps, and outputs
A new Application Menu module
A dictionary override on sys_flow
explanation: Custom Actions define inputs, internal steps, and outputs, becoming reusable building blocks within Flow Designer.

prompt: Which elements are required to compose a functioning Flow Designer flow? (Choose two.)
choices: A trigger that starts execution
One or more actions that perform steps
A transform map coalesce field
A client-side g_form API call
explanation: Every flow needs a trigger (record, schedule, etc.) and actions that execute the automation steps.

prompt: A developer needs a flow to run every Monday at 06:00 to summarize open tasks. Which trigger configuration applies?
choices: A record updated trigger on the task table only
An onSubmit client script on the task list
A before business rule with Display checked
A schedule trigger with weekly recurrence on Monday at 06:00
explanation: Schedule triggers let flows run on defined recurring intervals independent of record activity.

prompt: In a notification mail script, which object references the record that caused the notification to fire?
choices: g_form on the email template form
current
spModal in the portal
g_scratchpad in the browser
explanation: In notification mail scripts, current is the triggering GlideRecord, allowing field values to be inserted into the email body.

prompt: A purchase request flow must pause until the department manager approves, then continue to fulfillment tasks. Which Flow Designer feature should the developer use?
choices: A dictionary default value on the approver field
An onSubmit client script on the request form
An approval action that suspends the flow until approval completes
A transform map script on the staging table
explanation: Flow Designer approval actions pause execution until requested approvals are granted or rejected, then resume downstream steps.

prompt: A CSV file of asset records must be loaded into cmdb_ci_hardware. Where do imported rows land before transformation?
choices: Into the browser sessionStorage cache
Into an ACL record on the CI table
Directly into cmdb_ci_hardware without staging
A staging Import Set table linked to a transform map
explanation: Import Sets stage data in a dedicated table; a Transform Map then maps and loads rows onto the target table.

prompt: Column names in a spreadsheet match target field names on u_vendor. What utility maps them automatically in the transform map?
choices: Auto Map Matching Fields
CI Relationship Builder
Business Service Management Map
Coalesce Fields Only
explanation: Auto Map Matching Fields creates field maps when import set column names match target field names.

prompt: A transform map must update existing vendor records when u_vendor_id matches instead of inserting duplicates. Which setting enables this?
choices: Disable the transform map after the first run
Mark u_vendor_id as a coalesce field on the transform map
Delete the import set table between loads
Set every mapped field to read-only on the form
explanation: Coalesce fields tell the transform to match existing target records on that value and update them rather than inserting duplicates.

prompt: What does a Transform Map define during an import from staging to a target table?
choices: Which roles appear in the Application Navigator
The color scheme of the import data source form
Field mappings, optional scripts, and coalesce keys between staging and target
The schedule for Flow Designer approval steps
explanation: Transform Maps specify how staging columns map to target fields, including coalesce logic and transform scripts.

prompt: A Script Include must POST JSON to an external HR API from server code. Which API should the developer use?
choices: GlideAjax from an onChange client script
g_scratchpad to store the HTTP response
GlideForm client API from a business rule
sn_ws.RESTMessageV2 to build and execute the outbound request
explanation: RESTMessageV2 constructs and sends outbound REST requests from server-side scripts and returns the response for processing.

prompt: Before embedding REST calls in production scripts, a developer wants to test endpoint URLs, headers, and payloads interactively. Which tool helps?
choices: REST API Explorer or the REST Message Test action
Scheduled Job run history
Access Control security debugging
Form Designer layout preview
explanation: REST API Explorer and REST Message testing let developers configure and validate outbound requests before scripting them.

prompt: After executing RESTMessageV2.execute(), which methods retrieve the HTTP results? (Choose two.)
choices: getStatusCode()
addInfoMessage()
getBody()
setMandatory()
explanation: The REST response object exposes getBody() for the payload and getStatusCode() for the HTTP status; the others are unrelated client APIs.

prompt: A team needs no-code connectors to call third-party SaaS APIs from flows with reusable spokes and actions. Which platform capability fits?
choices: IntegrationHub spokes and actions
Dictionary overrides on sys_ws_operation
Inbound Email Actions only
Homepage gauges for integration metrics
explanation: IntegrationHub provides spokes and actions that encapsulate third-party API connectivity for use in flows and integrations.

prompt: A data team receives a spreadsheet of vendor contacts to load through an Import Set. Which format does ServiceNow accept for direct Import Set loading?
choices: Raw disk images
Encrypted password vault exports only
Excel (XLS/XLSX) or CSV
Compiled Java bytecode
explanation: Import Sets accept structured data files such as CSV and Excel, staging rows before transform to target tables.

prompt: An enterprise program needs centralized governance over scoped application ownership, health, and deployment pipelines across dev, test, and prod. Which tool provides this?
choices: Homepage gauge editor
App Engine Management Center (AEMC)
Inbound email configuration
Transform map history
explanation: App Engine Management Center offers centralized visibility and governance for scoped applications, pipelines, and instance promotion.

prompt: A scoped application team wants to commit Studio changes to a corporate Git repository and apply remote updates back to the instance. Which capability enables this?
choices: ServiceNow source control (Git) integration in Studio
Inbound email client configuration
Import set auto-mapping
Application Navigator module ordering
explanation: Studio's Git integration links a scoped app to an external repository for commit, branch, and apply-remote workflows.

prompt: An admin must let contractor developers edit Script Includes and business rules in one scoped app without granting admin. What should they configure?
choices: Convert the scoped app to global scope
Disable all ACLs on the application tables
Remove source control from the instance
Delegated Development permissions for specific file types in that application
explanation: Delegated Development assigns developers rights to specified application file types and optional code review without full admin access.

prompt: When managing files in a global application, which action is permitted?
choices: Adding global-scope files to the global application
Changing a global application to a scoped application
Removing scope from an installed scoped application
Moving scoped application files into global scope
explanation: Global applications can include global-scope files; you cannot move files across scopes, change global app scope, or remove an app's scope.

prompt: A developer finishes configuration changes on a sub-production instance and needs to bundle them for movement to test. Which mechanism captures the changes?
choices: A homepage gauge showing pending changes
An Update Set that records modified application files
An Import Set that stages CSV rows only
An ACL that grants write on sys_update_set
explanation: Update Sets group configuration changes so they can be completed, exported, retrieved, previewed, and committed on another instance.

prompt: A team completes an update set in development, retrieves it in test, previews the changes, and commits it in test. Which sequence reflects correct update set promotion?
choices: Complete in dev, retrieve in test, preview in test, commit in test
Commit in dev, delete in test, retrieve in prod, preview in dev
Preview in dev, retrieve in dev, complete in test, commit in prod only
Retrieve in dev, complete in test, commit without preview in prod
explanation: Update sets are completed on the source instance, retrieved on the target, previewed to review impact, then committed on the target.

prompt: How should a scoped application be moved to another instance when instances do not share an update source?
choices: Retype every table and script manually on the target
Email configuration screenshots to the target admin
Delete target instance tables before import
Publish to an application repository or Store and install on the target instance
explanation: Scoped apps are distributed by publishing to a repository or Store for installation, or via source control apply-remote on the target.

prompt: Which source control operations are available for a scoped app linked to Git in Studio? (Choose two.)
choices: Commit local changes to a branch
Rename the sys_user table globally
Disable the instance authentication realm
Apply remote repository changes into the instance
explanation: Git integration supports committing instance changes to a branch and applying remote changes back into the application on the instance.

prompt: Before deploying a downloaded Store application into production, what practice reduces risk?
choices: Disable every ACL on production before install
Install and validate the application in a sub-production instance first
Delete all existing scoped apps on production
Convert the application to global scope on production
explanation: Applications should be installed and tested in sub-production before production promotion to avoid disrupting live services.
